dataSource: One upstream only: Twelve Data REST GET https://api.twelvedata.com/time_series?symbol=<raw>&interval=<mapped>&outputsize=<10..500>&apikey=<TWELVE_DATA_API_KEY> (supabase/functions/get-candles/index.ts:220; key read at :5). There is no database, cache, fallback provider or service-role client. In production the TWELVE_DATA_API_KEY secret does not exist ('supabase secrets list' returns 17 names and this one is not among them). The function therefore never reaches Twelve Data and answers every POST with 503 'Service not configured' (index.ts:150-156). Crypto on /backtest does not use this function: the browser calls Binance public klines directly (src/pages/backtest.astro:363-378, :404).
howItWorks:
Runtime: deno std@0.177.0 serve (index.ts:2, :128). OPTIONS returns 204 with CORS headers (:133-138). Any method other than POST returns 405 (:142-147). Order of checks on a POST: API key present, else 503 (:150-156); in-memory rate limit (:159-177); JSON parse, 400 on failure (:180-188); only symbol, interval, limit and outputsize are read (:190); symbol is required and must match /^[A-Z0-9\/\.\-]{1,20}$/ on a trimmed, upper-cased copy (:16, :102-106, :193-207); interval mapping (:210-213); outputsize clamp (:216-217); upstream fetch with a 15 s abort timeout (:114-126, :224); error mapping (:226-261); response (:264-291).
SYMBOL MAPPING: none. The raw string is forwarded unencoded, so callers must already use Twelve Data notation (EUR/USD, XAU/USD). Broker names such as EURUSD, XAUUSD or US30 are not mapped. INSTRUMENT_TYPES (:17) is never used.
INTERVAL MAPPING (:20-30): 1min, 5min, 15min, 30min, 1h, 4h, 1d->1day, 1w->1week, 1m->1month. Unknown or missing values silently become '1day' with only a console.warn (:210-213). '15m', which the page sends, is not a key. validateInterval uses 'in', so prototype keys such as 'toString' pass (:110).
OUTPUTSIZE: outputsize || limit || 300, clamped to 10..500 (:216-217). Twelve Data allows up to 5000. There is no pagination.
DATE RANGES: not supported. start_date, end_date, date, timezone and order are neither read (:190) nor forwarded (:220), so the result is always the latest N bars up to now.
TIMEZONE: no timezone parameter is sent, so Twelve Data uses its default 'Exchange'. Datetime strings carry no offset, and meta.exchange_timezone is dropped (:264-274).
RESPONSE: 200 {symbol, interval, count, values, meta:{currency, exchange, type}}. values is Twelve Data's raw array: newest first, OHLC as strings, datetime 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss' (daily bars use 'YYYY-MM-DD'). Headers: X-RateLimit-* (:277-281) and Cache-Control 'public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300' (:289).
CACHING: effectively none. There is no server, DB or KV cache. Browsers and CDNs do not cache POST responses, and the service worker skips supabase.co (public/sw.js:48).
RATE LIMITING: fixed-window counter in a module-level Map (:33, :63-86), so it lives in one worker isolate. The key is '<jwt sub or anonymous>:<cf-connecting-ip | first x-forwarded-for | x-real-ip>' (:35-61). The sub is decoded with atob and no signature check (:45-57); that is safe only because the gateway verifies the JWT. Defaults are 30 requests per 60 s (:6-7; RATE_LIMIT_* are not set in prod). Counters are not shared across isolates or regions, reset when workers recycle and are never evicted.
CORS: the allowlist comes from the ALLOWED_ORIGINS secret (present in prod), else a fallback whose first entry is the placeholder 'https://your-domain.com' (:8-13). A disallowed origin gets ACAO=ALLOWED_ORIGINS[0], but its request is still processed. Allow-Headers is 'Content-Type, Authorization' only (:94). There is no Vary: Origin and no Expose-Headers.
AUTH: the gateway has verify_jwt=true. Any valid project JWT passes, including the public anon key, so no signed-in user is needed. The function never checks a user, plan or ownership, creates no Supabase client, does not use the service role and does no DB access.
ERRORS: 405; 503 when the key is missing; 429 with retry_after; 400 for bad JSON or a bad symbol; a non-2xx upstream status is passed through with 'Data service unavailable' (:226-235); a Twelve Data status:error becomes 503 for codes 401/403 and HTTP 400 with the upstream message and code for anything else, including credit exhaustion (:240-261); 504 on abort (:297-305); 500 with the raw error.message (:307-313).
TIMEOUT: 15 s on the upstream request (:224). The body read (:237) is not covered.
LOGGING: console.log on every request (:222); console.warn for unknown intervals (:212) and for rate-limit hits, including user id and IP (:163); console.error for the missing key (:151), upstream errors (:227, :241) and exceptions (:294).

replayFit:
It cannot serve as the replay data layer.
(a) Core features are missing. It returns only the latest ≤500 bars, with no range, pagination, timezone or ordering control, so resume-at-replay_time and go-to-date are impossible.
(b) Volume: one forex week of M1 is about 7,200 bars, roughly 0.7 MB in Twelve Data JSON. That is 15 calls at the function's 500 cap, or 2 calls at Twelve Data's 5,000 max.
(c) Rate limits: Twelve Data bills 1 credit per call. Basic allows 8 per minute and 800 per day for the whole app, since there is one shared key. One M1-week load through the current function uses about 2 minutes of the app-wide minute quota, and the daily quota covers about 53 such loads for all users together (about 400 with 5,000-bar pages). Grow (55/min, no daily cap) helps, but cost still grows with users × sessions.
(d) A shared server-side cache is therefore required. History never changes and is the same for every user, so provider cost drops to one backfill plus about 1 call per symbol per day. The backfill is about 490 calls per symbol for M1 since 2020-02-10, or about 3,900 for 7 majors plus XAU/USD: about 5 days of Basic quota, or about 71 minutes on Grow. Size: about 19-20M M1 rows (about 1.5-2 GB as plain rows with a PK index) or about 0.2-0.35 GB as compressed per-day chunks. The database is 15 MB today, has no candle table, and its only extensions are pg_stat_statements, pgcrypto, plpgsql, supabase_vault and uuid-ossp (no pg_cron, no pg_net).
(e) M1 depth: Twelve Data says 1-minute data starts on 2020-02-10. An older go-to-date target would have daily data only, or would need another source. Confirm per symbol with /earliest_timestamp.
(f) Gaps: providers return only bars that exist. That leaves out weekends (Fri ~21-22:00 UTC to Sun ~21-22:00 UTC), holidays, gold's daily break and quiet minutes. Replay must step bar by bar, and higher-timeframe candles must be bucketed by time. The new system must choose UTC or New-York-close alignment, which decides where H4/D1 boundaries fall relative to the user's broker.
(g) No-future rule: today the page loads every bar and reveals them in the browser (backtest.astro:644-648, :550-557), so future bars already sit in the browser. A strict rule needs the server to cut data off at the account's replay_time.
(h) Intra-bar TP/SL: building H1 from M1 and settling TP/SL ties with M1 works, but Twelve Data has nothing below 1min, so a tie inside a single M1 bar needs a fixed rule.
(i) USD P&L: the majors and XAU/USD all quote against USD, so the pair's own price converts the quote currency to USD. Spread has to be simulated because there is no bid/ask series, and commission is a configuration value.
providerFacts:
Twelve Data, checked 2026-10-18.
time_series: costs 1 credit per symbol. Intervals run from 1min to 1month (nothing below 1min). outputsize is 1-5000; the default is 30 without dates and the maximum when dates are given. start_date and end_date are supported (format 2006-01-02 or 2006-01-02T15:04:05; default location is UTC for forex and crypto). Other parameters: date, order asc|desc (default desc), and timezone Exchange (default)|UTC|IANA, which is ignored for intervals of 1day and above. datetime is the bar open in exchange time with no offset suffix, and meta includes exchange_timezone.
History: 1-minute OHLC exists only from 2020-02-10 (support article 5656039); daily data covers full history; /earliest_timestamp returns the first available date per symbol and interval.
Plans (the pricing page shows partly inconsistent prices):
- Basic: free, 8 credits/min, 800/day, 'Internal non-display usage'.
- Grow: 55/min (table), no daily limit, 'Internal display data access', includes 'Commodities market data'.
- Pro: 610/min.
- Ultra: 2,584/min.
The individual-plan header says 'personal, internal, and non-commercial purposes'. Indices are not mentioned for any plan.
Terms: internal use only (§1, §2.1); no commercial use of Free Tier data (§2.3(l)); external display or redistribution only with a Redistribution Rights add-on or a written agreement (§2.2(e), §2.4); data may be stored solely for internal use (§2.2(a)); no caching beyond permitted timeframes (§2.3(g)); data must be deleted within 30 days after termination (§16.2(a)).
Attribution ('Data provided by Twelve Data' with a dofollow link) is required when data is shown publicly in apps.

recommendation:
Rewrite. Do not extend get-candles; retire it with the old page. Production already cannot serve a single candle, so removing it costs current users nothing.
1. Remove:
   - the repo folder supabase/functions/get-candles/
   - the deployed slug get-candles
   - then the ALLOWED_ORIGINS secret, which none of the other five deployed functions reads.
   TWELVE_DATA_API_KEY is already absent, and RATE_LIMIT_* were never set (create-payment also reads them but only uses the defaults). Update PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md:168 and :290 and the page's data layer (src/pages/backtest.astro:355-406).
2. Before writing code, pick a data source and license that allow storing candles and showing them to paying users. Twelve Data needs a business or redistribution agreement. Alternatives worth evaluating include cTrader Open API trendbars and tick data via the existing cTrader integration, or another FX vendor. Confirm M1 depth per symbol, for example with Twelve Data /earliest_timestamp.
3. Build a shared, immutable candle store: for example a market_candles_m1 table keyed by (symbol, ts timestamptz UTC) with numeric OHLC, or per-symbol, per-day compressed chunks in Storage. Authenticated users can read it; only the service role can write.
4. Ingest only on the server. A service-role job backfills and tops up using start_date/end_date, outputsize=5000, timezone=UTC and order=ASC. It needs idempotent upserts and throttling that stays within the plan's credits per minute. Schedule it with pg_cron + pg_net (neither is installed today) or an external cron.
5. Serve replay through one read API (a Postgres RPC or a small edge function):
   - Inputs: account_id, symbol, from, to, base timeframe.
   - Output: ascending numeric arrays [epoch_s, o, h, l, c].
   - Cut 'to' off at the account's saved replay_time, so future bars never leave the server.
   - Build higher timeframes from M1 by time bucket (date_bin), so progressive HTF candles and LTF tie-breaks always agree.
   - Fetch in chunks (for example one trading day of M1), not one request per step.
6. Keep an instruments table: provider symbol mapping for broker names such as EURUSD and XAUUSD, pip size, contract size, quote currency, default spread and commission. Use a fixed rule (for example SL first) for TP/SL ties inside a single M1 bar.
7. If an edge function stays in the path:
   - verify the user JWT and check plan and account ownership;
   - allow 'authorization, x-client-info, apikey, content-type';
   - keep provider keys out of URLs and error bodies;
   - use a DB-backed limiter rather than an in-memory one.
report:
VERDICT: rewrite. get-candles is a thin, stateless proxy to Twelve Data time_series that can only return the latest ≤500 bars. In production it is broken twice over: the TWELVE_DATA_API_KEY secret is missing (503 on every POST), and its CORS Allow-Headers block the supabase-js call the page makes.

SOURCE AND MECHANICS (supabase/functions/get-candles/index.ts)
- Upstream: one request to https://api.twelvedata.com/time_series with the key in the query string (:220).
- Inputs: only symbol, interval, limit and outputsize are read (:190).
- Symbol: regex-validated on an upper-cased copy, then sent raw with no mapping (:16, :102-106).
- Interval: 9-entry map; unknown values silently become 1day, and '1m' means month (:20-30, :210-213).
- outputsize: defaults to 300, clamped to 10..500 (:216-217).
- No dates, timezone or order are sent, so the result is always the latest N bars.
- Response: Twelve Data's raw newest-first string rows plus {currency, exchange, type} meta (:264-274), with Cache-Control on a POST, which does nothing (:289).
- Rate limit: in-memory per isolate, 30/min per jwt-sub+IP (:33-86).
- CORS: allowlist from the ALLOWED_ORIGINS secret, placeholder fallback (:8-13); Allow-Headers is 'Content-Type, Authorization' (:94).
- Auth: gateway verify_jwt only, so the public anon key is enough. No user check, no service role, no DB.
- Errors: 400/405/429/503/504/500. Provider quota errors come back as 400 (:240-261), and raw exception messages are returned to the caller (:307-310).
- Timeout: 15 s on headers only (:114-126, :224).
- Logs: one line per request, and rate-limit warnings include user id and IP (:163, :222).

PAGE: src/pages/backtest.astro is the only caller (:380-401, invoke at :385-387, body {symbol, interval}). Crypto goes to Binance directly from the browser (:363-378). The page reverses the bars and parses datetimes as local time (:392-400), preloads every bar and reveals them client-side (:631-658, :550-557), checks SL before TP inside a bar (:539-548), and computes P&L in % (:493-499). The page's '15m' option silently yields daily bars.

PRODUCTION (6 calls in total; the anon key was never printed):
- Deployed: v44, updated 2026-08-24, verify_jwt=true. Its source equals HEAD apart from type annotations and the fallback origin list.
- Secrets: TWELVE_DATA_API_KEY absent; RATE_LIMIT_* absent; ALLOWED_ORIGINS present, contains https://wawejournal.com, and is read only by get-candles.
- Call results:
  - EUR/USD 1d: 503, 1134 ms
  - preflight: 204, but apikey and x-client-info not allowed
  - EUR/USD 1min: 503, 352 ms
  - XAU/USD 5min: 503, 382 ms
  - historical M1 week: 503, 311 ms
  - no-JWT call: gateway 401, 321 ms
- No candles came back, so candle counts and first/last timestamps could not be recorded.

PROVIDER: Twelve Data supports start_date/end_date, outputsize up to 5000, a timezone parameter (default Exchange) and 1 credit per call. 1-minute history exists only from 2020-02-10. Basic is 8 credits/min and 800/day and is licensed for internal, non-display, non-commercial use. External display needs a redistribution add-on or a written agreement, and stored data must be deleted 30 days after termination. Attribution is required.

FIT: a forex M1 week of about 7,200 bars costs 15 credits through this function, or 2 at the provider maximum. On Basic that means about 53 week-loads per day for the entire app. A shared, immutable candle cache plus server-side ingestion is mandatory; the backfill for M1 since 2020 on 8 symbols is about 3,900 calls. The DB has no candle table, is 15 MB, and has no pg_cron or pg_net. Gaps and weekends require bar-driven replay with time-bucketed HTF aggregation. A strict no-future rule needs server-side cut-off at replay_time. M1 is the finest tie-break the provider offers. USD P&L for majors and gold can use the pair's own price, but spread must be simulated.
